newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban drive Afghan troops back in counter-attack.
newsitem.headline: Taleban drive Afghan troops back in counter-attack.

text.p: Islamic Taleban rebels said they had advanced to within 15 km (nine miles) of the government-held town of Sarobi on the Kabul-Jalalabad highway on Monday, a Pakistan-based Afghan news agency reported.

A Taleban spokesman told the Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) that the Taleban had pushed their opponents back towards Sarobi, 70 km (40 miles) east of Kabul, in a fierce counter-attack after government troops made small gains in fighting on Sunday.
"We have advanced 15 to 20 km (nine to 13 miles) since yesterday," the spokesman told AIP.
He put Taleban casualties at four dead in the latest battle, but AIP said a higher number had been taken to Jalalabad, the eastern city captured by the Taleban on September 11.
There was no immediate word on government losses.
AIP said government troops had attacked Taleban positions near the town of Maidan Shahr, southwest of Kabul. The Taleban said they had repelled the assault after a three-hour battle.

A Taleban spokesman said earlier that the militia's military chief, Mullah Borjan, was expected to move to the Sarobi front soon after mopping up government resistance in Kunar province on the Pakistani border, which fell to the rebels on Sunday.
No comment from the government side was immediately available and there was no independent account of the fighting for Sarobi, which lies on the main road to Kabul.
The Taleban have tightened their grip on eastern provinces this month as part of their drive to seize the capital, oust President Burhanuddin Rabbani and impose a strict Islamic order.

Sarobi, a stronghold of Prime Minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar's Hezb-i-Islami faction, controls access to the Tagab Valley, a route for a possible assault on the government's main military airbase at Bagram, about 50 km (31 miles) north of Kabul.
